lights.detail: When you name a light, plug or fan yourself - "turn off the kitchen light" - Jarvis switches it without an approval card. Locks, doors, alarms, covers and garage doors always ask, each with a card of its own, and so does everything after Jarvis has read outside text in the chat. Turning this on shows you an approval card first; turning it off happens at once.
lights.label: Lights, plugs and fans without a card

lockdown.detail: One tap makes every way out of this PC ask you first, or stop: web search and research, sending or saving email, reading your calendar, email and Home Assistant, your smart home, news feeds and "tell me when" watches, plug-in programs, cloud AI models, chatbot conversations, the online weather behind the animal and checking for tool updates. Turning it on is instant, from either app. Turning it off is on the PC only, with an approval card and Windows Hello.
lockdown.label: Lockdown
lockdown.says: Lockdown is on: everything that would leave this PC asks you first, and anything that runs by itself ("tell me when", news, the briefing's calendar and email, chatbot conversations, the online weather) has stopped.

words.detail: Everything Jarvis can do that might need your OK, and whether it asks you first. The PC writes this list from its own settings - the AI model does not write it. "Ask me first" makes one ask every time, at once, from either app. Letting one go ahead without asking is only for the short list below, only on the PC, and takes an approval card and Windows Hello.
words.lights_detail: When you name a light, plug or fan yourself - "turn off the kitchen light" - Jarvis switches it without an approval card. Locks, doors, alarms, covers and garage doors always ask, each with a card of its own, and so does everything after Jarvis has read outside text in the chat. Turning this on shows you an approval card first; turning it off happens at once.
words.lights_label: Lights, plugs and fans without a card
words.lights_waiting: Waiting for your yes on the approval card, on your PC or phone.
words.lockdown_detail: One tap makes every way out of this PC ask you first, or stop: web search and research, sending or saving email, reading your calendar, email and Home Assistant, your smart home, news feeds and "tell me when" watches, plug-in programs, cloud AI models, chatbot conversations, the online weather behind the animal and checking for tool updates. Turning it on is instant, from either app. Turning it off is on the PC only, with an approval card and Windows Hello.
words.lockdown_off_says: Lockdown is off: everything asks first as your settings say.
words.lockdown_on_says: Lockdown is on: everything that would leave this PC asks you first, and anything that runs by itself ("tell me when", news, the briefing's calendar and email, chatbot conversations, the online weather) has stopped.
words.lockdown_pc_only: Lockdown can only be turned off on the PC (Settings, What asks first), with an approval card and Windows Hello.
words.lockdown_row_note: Lockdown is on, so this asks you first - or stops, if it runs by itself.
words.lockdown_waiting: Waiting for your yes on the approval card, and Windows Hello, on your PC.

no_switch_note.approve_web_search_for_conversation: This one rides with Web search: with Web search offered, the AI is offered this too, and without it this tool could not search anyway. It has no switch of its own, so nothing was changed here.
no_switch_note.cloud_escalation: This one is not a switch of its own: it rides with "Change one of Jarvis's own settings", and while that tool is offered the AI is offered this too. Its card is the Presets menu's Cloud row switch, so nothing was changed here.
no_switch_note.product_check: The product check has its own switch: the line [product_check] enabled = true in jarvis-framework.toml. That line is what offers this tool, so a line in [tools].enabled would change nothing. Nothing was changed here.
no_switch_note.run_data_script: The data and maths sandbox has its own switch: Settings, Data sandbox (or the sandbox row on the What asks first page). That switch is what offers this tool, so a line in [tools].enabled would change nothing. Nothing was changed here.
no_switch_note.stop_web_search_approval: This one rides with Web search: with Web search offered, the AI is offered this too. It has no switch of its own, so nothing was changed here.
